content.fundamental_principle: Interim period viewed as INTEGRAL PART of annual period (not discrete period)

revenues.recognition: Recognize in interim period when earned (same as annual)
revenues.seasonal_revenues: Report as earned, do NOT spread evenly over quarters. Disclose seasonal nature.

costs_and_expenses.costs_associated_with_revenue: Match to revenue in period recognized (same as annual)

other_costs_and_expenses.allocated_costs: Allocate among interim periods based on estimate of time, sales volume, or activity (e.g., depreciation, property tax, advertising)
other_costs_and_expenses.example_property_tax: Annual property tax $12K paid in Q2 → Allocate $3K to each quarter (Q1 accrue $3K, Q2 record $12K payment and reverse $3K accrual, etc.)

inventory_and_cogs.gross_profit_method_allowed: May use gross profit method or other estimation for interim periods (physical count not required each quarter)

lifo_liquidation.if_temporary: If LIFO layer liquidated temporarily (expect to replace by year-end), charge COGS at expected replacement cost (not lower LIFO cost)
lifo_liquidation.example: Q1 liquidates 100 units LIFO at $5/unit cost. Expect to replace at $8/unit by year-end. Q1 COGS = 100 × $8 = $800 (not $500). Create liability 'Excess of replacement cost over LIFO' $300.

inventory_loss.market_decline: If inventory market value decline is temporary, do NOT write down in interim period. If permanent, write down.
inventory_loss.example: Inventory cost $100K, market $90K in Q2. If expect recovery by year-end → no write-down in Q2. If decline is permanent → write down $10K in Q2.

income_taxes.effective_tax_rate_approach: Use estimated annual effective tax rate (AETR) for interim period tax expense
calculation_steps: 1. Estimate total annual ordinary income and tax
2. Calculate AETR = Estimated annual tax / Estimated annual ordinary income
3. Interim tax expense = YTD ordinary income × AETR
4. Current quarter tax = YTD tax - Prior quarters' tax
income_taxes.temporary_differences: Deferred taxes recognized in interim periods
income_taxes.discrete_items: Unusual or infrequent items (not extraordinary) may be recognized entirely in the quarter incurred

tax_calculation_example.facts: Q1 ordinary income $100K. Estimated annual ordinary income $500K. Estimated annual tax expense $120K (includes $20K permanent differences). Q2 ordinary income $150K (YTD $250K).

special_items.change_in_accounting_principle: Apply retrospectively (restate prior interim periods if practicable)
special_items.change_in_estimate: Apply prospectively starting in quarter of change
special_items.contingencies: Recognize if probable and estimable (same as annual)
special_items.discontinued_operations: Report separately in interim period of disposal decision

disclosures: Significant changes in estimates or provisions for income taxes
Disposal of segment and unusual or infrequent items
Changes in accounting principles or estimates

comparison_to_annual.same_accounting_principles: Use same accounting principles as annual statements
comparison_to_annual.more_estimation: More estimates permitted (e.g., gross profit method for inventory, property tax allocation)
comparison_to_annual.integral_view: Costs and expenses allocated across quarters (not treated as separate discrete periods)

cpa_exam_tips: Integral view: Allocate costs like property tax, advertising across all quarters
Seasonal revenues: Report when earned, don't spread evenly
Interim tax: Use estimated annual effective tax rate (AETR)
Temporary LIFO liquidation: Charge COGS at replacement cost if expect to replace
Temporary inventory decline: Don't write down if expect recovery
Gross profit method OK for interim inventory valuation

interim_tax: Always calculate AETR first (annual tax / annual income)
Apply AETR to YTD ordinary income
Current quarter = YTD tax - prior quarters' tax
property_tax_allocation: Accrue expense evenly even if payment occurs in one quarter
LIFO_liquidation: If temporary: Use replacement cost for COGS

common_traps: Don't spread seasonal revenue evenly across quarters
Don't forget to subtract prior quarters' tax when calculating current quarter
Temporary vs permanent distinctions for LIFO liquidation and inventory write-downs

key_points: Integral view: Interim period is part of annual period (allocate costs)
Seasonal revenues reported when earned (not smoothed)
Interim tax uses estimated annual effective tax rate (AETR)
Temporary LIFO liquidation: COGS at replacement cost
Temporary inventory decline: Don't write down
Gross profit method permitted for interim inventory
